rationale: Final named item of the open gap: the sweep now records a liveness witness. After each event's invariant checks it asks whether any node still has a committed-but-unapplied configuration change and, in that case, whether any node is promotable (able to campaign); when the answer is 'unapplied present and nothing promotable' it counts a stalled state, and invariant_sweep_summary reports stalled_states. Draft-side this revision reports seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=466, ordinary proposals=452, conf_change_proposals=249, restarts=471, stalled_states=0, violations=0, so in this event set the guard never left the configuration without a voter able to campaign while a configuration change was pending. That is exactly the kind of bounded-liveness statement the task asks for, but it is a zero count over a fixed event set and construction feedback only, so the experiment below requests isolated execution of these bytes; if the receipt also reports stalled_states=0, the number bounds nothing beyond this event set, and if it is non-zero the decisive operands are the seed, step and node states, which the summary alone would not carry, so a follow-up would have to emit them per occurrence.

scope.description: Eighth revision of the same fixed harness; probes A, B and C are unchanged. The sweep keeps four real state machines (ids 1..4, node 4 registered directly with the network and starting outside the configuration), single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals on node 4 half of the time with Transition=JointImplicit, committed conf changes applied through applyConfChange, and restart events that rebuild a random node from its persisted hard state and applied ConfState. New in this revision: after each event the harness evaluates a liveness witness - if any node has a committed-but-unapplied configuration change, it checks whether any of the four nodes is promotable, and counts a stalled state when none is - and invariant_sweep_summary now reports stalled_states alongside seeds, steps, elections, proposals, conf_change_proposals, restarts and violations.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, hasUnappliedConfChanges, promotable, newRaft); no production logic is modified.
The witness uses the target's own predicates for the two conditions it combines, so it measures the state the campaign guard reacts to rather than a reimplementation of it.
A state is only counted when both conditions hold simultaneously at the check point between events.
Counts over a fixed seed set are descriptive, not rates.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup on a random node, MsgProp with a tagged payload, tick() on a random node, isolate a random node, recover, TransferLeader from a random voter to the current leader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change on node 4, half the time JointImplicit), a restart of a random node from its persisted hard state and applied ConfState, or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4, evaluate the four invariants, then evaluate the liveness witness (any node with committed-but-unapplied conf changes while no node is promotable) and finally emit invariant_sweep_summary with all counters including stalled_states.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and sweep case as the previous execution, with the liveness witness added: the harness now counts states where a node holds a committed-but-unapplied configuration change while no node is promotable, using the target's own hasUnappliedConfChanges and promotable predicates, and reports stalled_states in the summary. This is the last item the open gap named. Fresh execution is requested because the harness bytes and the reported fields changed.
